title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Ava Chen
summary: Consolidated company handbook reference covering ways of working, role families and career ladders, promotion and review cadence, benefits and perks, hiring and onboarding workflow, and core internal tools.
content:
Overview

This page is the canonical single-page handbook reference for working at Redwood. It provides a high-level summary of our ways of working, role families and career ladders, promotion and performance review practices, benefits and perks, the standard hiring and onboarding workflow, and the primary internal tools you will use. People Ops maintains this page and reviews it quarterly.

1) Redwood culture & ways of working

- Mission focus: ship predictable, economical inference for production. Teams prioritize customer-impacting work and measurable outcome metrics.
- Principles: ship small, measure early, prefer automation over manual ops, and default to empathy and radical clarity in communication.
- Working model: remote-first with optional office hubs in major regions. Be mindful of asynchronous collaboration across NA/EU/APAC; schedule recurring syncs with timezone sensitivity when needed.
- Communication norms: Slack for realtime coordination, Confluence for long-lived documents and runbooks, and GitHub PRs for technical changes. Use calendar blocks for deep work.

2) Role families and career ladders (summary)

Each function maintains a detailed ladder document linked in the related pages section. The summary below is intended to guide managers and ICs when setting expectations and preparing promotion packets.

- Engineering (SWE):
  - IC1 / Associate Engineer: delivers well-scoped tasks, writes maintainable code, and fixes bugs with supervision.
  - IC2 / Engineer: independently delivers features, owns components, participates in design reviews, and writes tests.
  - Senior Engineer: leads cross-service designs, mentors colleagues, owns reliability and observability improvements.
  - Staff / Principal Engineer: sets architecture for large systems, leads multi-quarter initiatives, and impacts product direction.

- Product & PM:
  - Associate PM: assists scoping and execution for a product sub-area.
  - PM: owns a feature area, defines requirements and success metrics, and coordinates delivery.
  - Senior PM: drives roadmap, stakeholder alignment, and cross-functional rollouts with measurable outcomes.

- Applied ML / Research:
  - Research Engineer / Applied ML: implements evals, supports model onboarding, and measures production quality.
  - Senior Applied ML: defines evaluation strategy, quality guardrails, and production validation processes.

- SRE / Infra / Runtime:
  - SRE Engineer: manages SLOs, runbooks, and incident response for services.
  - Senior SRE / Infra Engineer: owns capacity planning, reliability initiatives, and platform improvements for autoscaling and cost control.

- Customer Success & Support:
  - Customer Success Manager: owns onboarding and QBRs for named accounts and coordinates post-sale technical delivery.
  - Senior CSM / Solutions Engineer: leads complex integrations, negotiates SLA commitments, and manages escalations.

- People Ops, Finance, Sales, Design: similar level distinctions (Associate, Professional, Senior, Lead) with function-specific competencies and examples captured in their ladder documents.

3) Promotion criteria and examples of evidence

Promotions are granted based on demonstrated impact, scope of ownership, craft and execution, leadership and collaboration, and operational reliability. Typical evidence included in a promotion packet:

- Statement of expanded scope and desired level.
- Three to five concrete examples (PRs, releases, incident responses, customer outcomes) showing the candidate operating at the target level.
- Peer and manager feedback, and 1-2 quantitative metrics where applicable (e.g., latency reduction, cost savings, improved deployment success rate).
- Manager write-up mapping the candidate to level criteria.

People Ops publishes the promotion calendar each quarter; managers should schedule calibration with peers and the level-gate committee prior to submission.

4) Performance reviews and career development

- Cadence: company-wide performance reviews twice per year (mid-year and year-end) with manager write-ups and calibration sessions.
- Development planning: employees maintain a 30-60-90 plan and an annual development plan reviewed during manager 1:1s and performance reviews.
- Mentorship and learning: People Ops supports mentor matching and learning stipends for conferences, courses, and books.

5) Benefits & perks (high level)

Health & financial
- Medical, dental, and vision plans with multiple tiers and employer contributions.
- Retirement benefits: 401(k) with employer match in the US and equivalent local plans internationally.
- Equity: competitive equity grants at hire and milestone refreshes during significant promotions or retention events.

Time off & family
- PTO: flexible paid time off; recommended minimum of 20 days plus company holidays.
- Parental leave: 18 weeks primary leave, 8 weeks secondary leave, phased return guidance and caregiver support.
- Flexible work hours and paid family leave top-ups where local laws allow.

Wellbeing & learning
- Monthly wellness stipend for fitness, therapy, or wellness subscriptions.
- Learning & development stipend (typical US allocation $1,500/year) for conferences, courses, and books.
- Home office stipend for ergonomic equipment and replacement cycle guidance.

Perks & support
- Commuter/office stipends where applicable, catered lunches during in-person offsites, and recognition programs.
- Employee assistance program (EAP) and access to legal/financial counseling resources.

6) Hiring process & interview guidelines (overview)

Standard hiring flow:
1. Requisition submitted by hiring manager with a scorecard and hiring rubric.
2. Recruiter sourcing and initial screen; qualified candidates advanced to hiring manager review.
3. Interview loop: recruiter screen, hiring manager screen, technical or role-specific interviews, and a final cross-functional or leadership assessment.
4. Debrief and calibrated decision using the scorecard.
5. Offer prepared by People Ops and approved by hiring manager.
6. Background checks and references initiated per local law after verbal acceptance.
7. Onboarding kickoff scheduled once clearances complete.

Interviewer best practices:
- Use the scorecard and focus on competencies and evidence.
- Ask behaviorally-anchored questions and probe for specific examples.
- Submit feedback within 48 hours.
- Avoid illegal or off-limits topics; consult People Ops with questions.

7) New hire onboarding: pre-start, day 1, week 1, 30/60/90

Pre-start (People Ops / IT):
- Provision accounts (Okta/SAML), order and ship equipment, grant base-level GitHub/Slack/Confluence access.
- Welcome packet with first-week agenda, team contacts, and pre-reading.

Day 1:
- Orientation led by People Ops covering mission, org overview, core policies, and benefits enrollment.
- Manager 1:1 to review role expectations and the 30/60/90 plan.
- Team onboarding: introductions to codebase, services, and immediate priorities.

Week 1:
- Complete access requests and verify dev environment (local build, CI).
- Complete mandatory security and compliance training.
- Assigned buddy for first 90 days to help with operational questions and cultural context.
- Ship a small first deliverable (doc, test, or small code change).

30/60/90 checkpoints:
- 30 days: comfortable with the dev environment and basic contribution merged.
- 60 days: independent ownership of a small feature or operational area.
- 90 days: measurable contribution to a team initiative and a career-development check-in.

8) Internal tools & where to get help (owners)

Primary tools used at Redwood and typical owners:
- Okta (People Ops / Security): single sign-on for company apps.
- Google Workspace (People Ops / IT): email, calendar, and Drive.
- Slack (Eng & Ops): realtime messaging and incident coordination; use channels for team and product discussions.
- Confluence (People Ops / Eng-Docs): source of truth for policies, design docs, runbooks, and onboarding materials.
- GitHub (Eng Platform): source code, PRs, CI pipelines; follow CODEOWNERS and PR template guidance.
- Jira (Eng Platform / Product): issue tracking, sprint planning, and roadmaps.
- HR portal (People Ops): benefits enrollment, time-off requests, payroll, and onboarding tasks.
- Expenses tool (Finance): submit reimbursements within 60 days with receipts attached.

Security & access guidance:
- MFA required for all accounts. Never share credentials.
- Request least privilege; use short-lived roles for elevated access.
- Use the secrets manager for credentials; never commit secrets to source code.
- For emergency elevated access, follow the on-call escalation runbook and submit an Access Request for time-limited permissions.

9) Day-to-day expectations and support model

- On-call responsibilities: teams publish rotation schedules and runbooks in Confluence. Engineers participate per team policy; CSMs follow customer escalation playbooks for account-impacting incidents.
- Development cadence: open PRs early for review, keep PRs reasonably sized (aim for <500 LOC), and include test coverage and rollout notes.
- Meetings: default to asynchronous updates where possible; keep synchronous meetings time-boxed and inclusive for remote participants.
